subject: general
question: If an object is kept at the focus F of a convex lens, where will the image be formed?

options.text: At 2F, real and same size as object
Between F and 2F, real and magnified

solution:
The correct answer is __**At infinity, highly magnified, real**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• When an object is placed exactly at the **Principal Focus (F1)** of a **convex lens**, the refracted rays emerge **parallel** to each other.
 
• Since **parallel rays** are considered to meet at **infinity**, the image is formed at an infinite distance from the **optical center** of the lens. ***Hence, the location of the image is at infinity.***
 
• The nature of the image formed by a **convex lens** in this scenario is **real and inverted**. In optics, a **real image** is formed when light rays actually converge at a point. ***Hence, the nature is real.***
